chunks: about a man who is killed in the path of Allah: should he be washed, shrouded, and embalmed with ḥanūṭ?

He said: 'He is buried as he is, in his clothes and with his blood, unless there remains in him a sign of life. If there remains in him a sign of life and then he dies, then he is to be washed, shrouded, embalmed with ḥanūṭ, and the funeral prayer is to be performed over him, because the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله prayed over Ḥamzah, shrouded him, and embalmed him, because he had been stripped.'

key_terms.جُرِّدَ: he was stripped of his clothing
key_terms.فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ: in the path of Allah; indicating martyrdom in Allah’s cause
key_terms.يُحَنَّطُ: he is embalmed with ḥanūṭ for burial
key_terms.يُصَلَّى عَلَيْهِ: the funeral prayer is performed over him
key_terms.يُغَسَّلُ: he is washed ritually before burial
key_terms.يُكَفَّنُ: he is shrouded in burial cloth

ai.seo_question: Does a martyr killed in the path of Allah receive ghusl and kafan before burial?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning one killed in the path of Allah. If he dies immediately, he is buried in his blood and clothes without ghusl, shrouding, or ḥanūṭ; but if life remains and he later dies, the normal rites of washing, shrouding, embalming, and funeral prayer apply. The report also cites the action of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله toward Ḥamzah as precedent.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.444 - Aban ibn Taghlib asked Him
about a man who is killed in the path of Allah (swt): Should he be washed, shrouded, and embalmed (with Hunut)?"

Imam (as) replied: "He should be buried as he is, in his clothing with his blood, unless there is a sign of life remaining. If he has a sign of life and then dies, he should be washed, shrouded, embalmed, and the funeral prayer should be offered for him. This is because the Messenger of Allah (sw) prayed over Hamza, shrouded him, and embalmed him because he had been stripped (of his clothing)”.
